neighbours.label: the possessive clitic 's / ' after a name or noun (weak, mostly gate-closed pole)
fire: We borrowed my neighbour's ladder to fix the gutter on Saturday.
The committee's report was published late on Friday afternoon.
He replaced the wheels with a set of Stan's rims before the race.
Everyone agreed that the chef's soup was the best dish of the night.
The players' union rejected the league's latest offer on salaries.
Visitors queued outside the museum's new wing for over an hour.
She found her grandmother's letters hidden in an old shoebox.
The council's decision surprised residents of the eastern district.
quiet: We borrowed a ladder from the neighbour to fix the gutter on Saturday.
The report of the committee was published late on Friday afternoon.
He replaced the wheels with a set of carbon rims before the race.
Everyone agreed that the soup from the chef was the best dish of the night.
The union of players rejected the latest offer from the league on salaries.
Visitors queued outside the new wing of the museum for over an hour.
She found letters from her grandmother hidden in an old shoebox.
The decision of the council surprised residents of the eastern district.

notes: Gate-closed regime dominates (61%); + pole of the same unit also peaks on 's, so this pole may be weak in live text.
